title: They didn’t leave God.
paragraphs:
They didn’t leave God.
They just chose comfort.
And that’s what makes it dangerous.

Because it doesn’t feel like rebellion…
It feels like rest.

You still believe.
Still attend.
Still say “Lord.”

You remember when His voice was loud.
When conviction hit like lightning.
When obedience was costly… but clear.

Not because God stopped speaking—
but because comfort started drowning Him out.

“I’m just tired.”
“I’ll obey later.”
“It’s not that serious.”

But deep down…
you felt it.
Here’s the truth most won’t say:
Comfort can become a hiding place for disobedience.

You can sit in comfort
while your calling suffocates beside you.
“If anyone would come after Me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow Me.” — Luke 9:23

Deny yourself.
Take up your cross.
Follow Me.
Some scholars interpret this “daily cross” as the ongoing surrender of personal will—choosing God’s way over comfort, every single day.

Not once.
Not when it’s easy.
And here’s where it cuts deep:
You don’t need to hate God to drift from Him.
You just need to love comfort a little more than obedience.

Your private compromises.
Your delayed obedience.
Your quiet resistance.

Not with condemnation—
but with clarity.
And this is where shame tries to take over.

“You’ve gone too far.”
“You had your chance.”
“You knew better.”
That voice is not from your Savior.

Because Jesus does not expose you to destroy you.
He exposes you to redeem you.
“But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”

Not when you were consistent.
Not when you were on fire.
Not when you were obedient.

You sinned.
Not just in action—but in affection.

You chose comfort over calling.
Self over surrender.
Silence over obedience.
And sin separates us from God.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23

That includes quiet sin.
Respectable sin.
Comfortable sin.
But God didn’t leave you there.

He lived the life you couldn’t live—perfect, obedient, surrendered.
Then He died the death you deserved.

Not as a symbol.
Not as a story.
“For Christ also suffered once for sins, the righteous for the unrighteous, that He might bring us to God.” — 1 Peter 3:18

Because comfort didn’t win.
Sin didn’t win.
Death didn’t win.
“Repent, therefore, and turn back, that your sins may be blotted out.” — Acts 3:19
God is not asking for perfection.

Not tomorrow.
Not when you feel ready.

Not dead.
Just buried under comfort.
And Jesus is standing at the edge of it…

To lay down the comfort that numbed your conviction
and pick up the cross that leads to life.

Because the same grace that saved you
is the grace that restores you.
If you feel this in your spirit, don’t ignore it.
